newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 30.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Many stocks will gain long-term attractiveness in the wake of the first Federal income-tax-cut package in 16 years.
* The Federal budget deal eliminates capital gains taxes for most homeowners.
* Kessler and Koop urged the White House to review industry documents before endorsing the proposed tobacco pact.
* UPS won a legislative victory as a House committee voted to block expansion of a rival U.S. Postal Service air export delivery service.
* McDonald's yanked the plum assignment of lead advertising agency from Leo Burnett after 15 years, and handed it to DDB Needham.

* U.S. West's $2.3 billion plan to sell its cellular business to AirTouch suffered a major setback after the companies appeared to lose their bid to win an exemption from new laws that end certain tax-free transactions.
* Northwest Air is close to signing an agreement in principle with KLM Royal Dutch Airlines that would apparently resolve the problems that have roiled their five-year alliance.
* Labor costs rose a tame 0.8 percent in the second quarter.
* The Dow Jones Industrials rose 53.42 to a record 8174.53.
* Citicorp is gearing up for a major cost-cutting campaign.
* Smith Barney will pay the government $1.05 million to settle to civil charges connected to the gift of a $2,200 Super Bowl ticket to ex-USDA chief Espy.
* Columbia/HCA's resignations will not slow or derail the criminal investigation of the hospital firm.
* Yahoo! and Visa ended their joint venture and announced a broadened partnership in electronic commerce.
* The Treasury market shrugged off early weakness to finish higher on a mix of positive economic data.

* Omega Advisors, a $4 billion money management firm, has snapped up more than two million shares of Columbia/HCA in the last two weeks, despite the massive federal fraud investigation the company is facing.
